deletion_validation.note: Related regression run preceded the final OS-store missing-entry safeguard; the six focused cases below include it.

checks: Three-page shell opens on tasks and conversation, with advanced tools kept out of main navigation
Empty state, capability handoff and authenticated local sync
Connection form, actual HTTP smoke, automatic local coordinator/workers, escaped cards, password clearing and mobile layout
Per-connection target shares validate to 100%, persist through real API, and remain distinct from observed token use
adversarial: quick task, chair-selected roles, explicit confirmation and automatic workers complete frozen independent checks
cooperative: quick task, chair-selected roles, explicit confirmation and automatic workers complete frozen independent checks
Task inbox combines briefing and execution, real API token receipts drive connection/task shares, rolling period selector, light/dark/mobile layouts
Installed CLI path fallback and OpenCode 2 guidance
Antigravity/legacy Google options and independent Codex/Claude profile creation, selected official-login routing, escaped labels and no password ingestion
Delete connection through confirmation dialog and authenticated API; shared official login remains available
Immediate terminate button closes a live API request, cancels queued work and shows actual worker exit acknowledgement
Offline worker cancellation stays unconfirmed; the UI does not claim all tokens or provider-side generation stopped
Unknown-only usage remains unknown in both the authenticated aggregate and the visible percentage
browser.disclosure: TEST-ONLY scripted CLI and local API model replies. HTTP, native workers, training, verification, restart and archive replay are real; no external account or model quality verified.

limitations: No real OpenCode Go subscription or user account was authenticated in automated testing. Native CLI/model API integration uses the real Linux client and a local scripted model service; Windows discovery is covered by platform tests.
Deleting a connection does not prove an outstanding provider call stopped. Active leases, uncertainty and missing native receipts block deletion after pausing new claims.
Official-client login profiles, historical tasks, job receipts and token usage are preserved. User-owned environment variables are not removed.
